Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap + next step: dedicated pool deep-dive
Attachments: redwood-capacity-worksheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), network-topology.png (image/png)

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call: 

Summary:
- Use case: low-latency document summarization and retrieval for agent-assisted workflows.
- Expected production traffic: baseline ~50 QPS, anticipated daily peak bursts up to ~250 QPS for 30–45s windows.
- Latency targets: target P50 ~60ms, P95 sub-300ms (end-to-end for single-turn completion).
- Data controls: VPC-only deployment preferred; SOC2 evidence will be requested during procurement.

Requested artifacts we attached: redwood-capacity-worksheet.xlsx (fill in per-endpoint QPS, avg tokens, burst windows) and a blank network-topology.png for your infra team to annotate.

Next step: schedule a dedicated pool sizing call (throughput & latency deep-dive) with our solutions engineering team so we can map traffic patterns to GPU pool configuration and queuing/batching strategies. Proposed 60-minute slots (PT):
- Thu Mar 11, 10:00–11:00
- Thu Mar 11, 14:00–15:00
- Fri Mar 12, 09:00–10:00

If none of the above work, suggest two alternatives and we’ll coordinate. On the call we’ll want someone from your infra/ops to validate network egress and tokenization assumptions.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(j) 415-555-0123

---
Note: attached worksheet is a short template — filling the avg tokens and peak windows will materially change pool recommendations.

From: Sophie Jones <sophie.jones@finlytics.com>

Date: 2027-03-09T18:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next step: dedicated pool deep-dive

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap and the artifacts. Alex (our infra lead) is looped in. A couple of clarifications from our side before the sizing call: 

- The 50 QPS baseline is accurate for our US region (we also have an EU staging region but won’t need dedicated capacity there initially).
- Peak bursts are primarily caused by nightly batch kicks and some marketing-driven spikes; when you say 30–45s bursts, that aligns with what we see.
- Latency: 300ms P95 is our hard requirement for interactive flows; we can tolerate higher for background jobs.

Availability (PT):
- Thu Mar 11: 14:00–15:00 is ideal for both Alex and me.
- Fri Mar 12: morning is possible but prefer Thu.

We also uploaded a rough token-per-request estimate to the drive link (see Google Drive) and Alex will annotate the network-topology.png with our egress paths.

Sophie
Sophie Jones
Head of Product — FinLytics
sophie.jones@finlytics.com
Office: +1-617-555-0184
